To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new analytical procedure for breath analysis has been proposed and successfully applied to heart failure (HF).

(i) a new analytical method for the analysis of exhalation VOCs has been developed and validated, which can be used to monitor the clinical conditions of HF patients, (ii) acetone is a potential biomarker of HF, and (iii) a significant decrease of the acetone levels in exhaled breath is observed at discharge, compared to the admission, in about 80% of HF patients, thus making this biomarker eligible to monitor the clinical status of HF patients.

(i) a new method for the analysis of breath volatile organic compounds based on needle trap micro-extration coupled with gas chromatographic-tandem mass spectroscopy has been developed, (ii) this method has been applied to analyze breath samples from heart failure patients, (iii) the analysis of breath acetone has been found to be a reliable marker of HF exacerbation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of a new analytical technique, NTME, to breath analysis in HF patients, with the aim to identify new biomarkers that may help in the management of this pathology.
the development of an analytical method based on NTME and GC–MS/MS for breath VOC analysis, with the aim to provide a useful tool for the noninvasive diagnosis and monitoring of HF.
the development and validation of a new analytical method that can be applied to breath analysis for clinical purposes, and the identification of a new biomarker of HF.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NTME-GC-MS/MS approach is a reliable, simple, fast and low cost method that can be applied to breath analysis, and in particular to the study of HF exacerbations.
the NTME technique is a powerful tool for the analysis of VOCs in breath and that the results of this study confirm its potential as a diagnostic tool in HF patients.
the proposed method is reliable and robust, and it can be applied for breath analysis in clinical practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NTME coupled with gas chromatographic separation and tandem mass spectrometric detection is an efficient tool for the analysis of breath VOCs, and it is suitable for clinical applications.
the breath acetone level could be used as a biomarker for the assessment of the HF exacerbation.
breath acetone is a promising biomarker of heart failure, and that NTME is an effective tool to analyze exhaled breath samples for clinical purposes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NTME coupled with gas chromatograpy-tandem mass spectroscopy is an effective and reliable method to analyze breath samples and to detect biomarkers of HF exacerbation in a clinical setting.
breath acetone is a promising candidate for monitoring HF patients.
the proposed NTME method can be used to monitor VOCs in exhaled breath, thus opening new avenues for the development of breath tests for the diagnosis and monitoring of several diseases.
